name: Biotin-Thiamine-Responsive Basal Ganglia Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Biotin-Thiamine-Responsive Basal Ganglia Disease Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Subacute encephalopathy with movement disorders including dystonia and parkinsonism
Bilateral symmetric lesions in the basal ganglia on MRI
Clinical improvement with biotin and thiamine supplementation
Identification of pathogenic variants in the SLC19A3 gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of subacute encephalopathy with basal ganglia lesions on MRI and clinical response to biotin and thiamine
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical and radiological criteria are met.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bilateral basal ganglia lesions on MRI

laboratory: Elevated lactate may be present during acute episodes
imaging: Bilateral symmetric T2 hyperintensities in basal ganglia on MRI
Possible involvement of thalami and cerebral cortex in severe cases
genetic: Pathogenic variants in SLC19A3 gene encoding thiamine transporter 2
other: Marked clinical improvement after initiation of biotin and thiamine therapy

distinguishingFeatures: History of alcohol abuse or malnutrition
Rapid response to thiamine alone without biotin
MRI lesions predominantly in mammillary bodies and periaqueductal gray
Multisystem involvement including muscle biopsy abnormalities
Genetic testing revealing mitochondrial DNA mutations

redFlags: Failure to respond to biotin and thiamine supplementation
Development of respiratory failure or coma
references: Hannah MJ et al. Biotin-thiamine-responsive basal ganglia disease: clinical features and treatment outcomes. Neurology. 2015;85(4):356-362.
Ozand PT et al. Biotin-responsive basal ganglia disease: a novel entity. Brain. 1998;121(6):1267-1279.
